newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts this week - Two rate meets and an auction.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts this week - Two rate meets and an auction.

text.p: Gilts will await the outcome of Monday's meeting of UK monetary authorities with interest but it is the risk of a rise in U.S. interest rates this week that will really keep the market spellbound, analysts said.
The U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meets on Tuesday, with a 25 basis point hike in the federal funds rate widely expected to follow.
"The odds have shifted towards a rate rise in the U.S.," said Nigel Richardson, Yamaichi International's head of bond research. "Market expectations have shifted towards that too."
Last week, a senior Federal Reserve official told Reuters that eight of the 12 district banks in the Federal Reserve System have requested a hike in official interest rates.
But with the U.S. bond market pricing in a small rate rise, a turning point in the U.S. interest rate cycle may not prompt the bond bloodbath that 1994's rate increase did.
"It won't help the bond markets but Europe should outperform the U.S. after a rise," Richardson said.
Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke and Bank of England Governor Eddie George hold the UK's monthly monetary meeting on Monday.

"While the political backdrop would appear to rule out a pre-emptive tightening, the Bank governor is becoming increasingly vocal in calling for higher interest rates," said Jonathan Philpotts, UK economist at Schroders.
"It is perhaps no longer correct to say that all the risks surrounding base rates are on the downside."
But Richardson said the only event capable of prompting a pre-election rate rise would be a calamitous slide for sterling.
Aside from interest rates, the gilt market will focus its attention on Wednesday's gilt auction. The Bank of England will sell 3.0 billion stg of 8.0 percent gilts due 2021.
Richardson said the long end of the gilt market is traditionally the preserve of domestic UK investors.
"The auction will go reasonably well but it might require some cheapening first," he said. "We're looking for a bit of downside going into it."

But with the gilt/Bund spread at 179 basis points as the UK market lags its European counterparts, further underperformance will be limited. "Anything above 180 basis points will see the spread retrace," Richardson said.
In terms of UK data, this week offers strictly second division releases.
Final second quarter GDP data are due on Tuesday, including balance of payments figures for the quarter and whole world and non-EU trade figures follow on Thursday.
Analysts at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell forecast the trade deficit for the year as a whole will virtually double last year's 2.9 billion stg deficit.
They also forecast a smaller, 800 million stg global trade deficit in July. But neither figure is likely to stir the gilt market.
